_comment: What the `skia-safe` prebuilt actually carries, and the notices Montagent owes for it.
This file exists because `cargo about` cannot see any of it. `skia-bindings`' manifest says
`license = "MIT"` — that is the licence of the *Rust binding code*. The thing that reaches a
release archive is a prebuilt static library (`libskia.a` / `skia.lib`) downloaded from
`rust-skia/skia-binaries`, and inside it are Skia itself under BSD-3-Clause plus five
third-party C/C++ libraries Skia vendors. A manifest-reading tool reports none of them.
`bundled` is derived rather than asserted: `ci/assert_third_party_attribution.py` reads the
member names out of whichever prebuilt is present in `target/` and checks that the set here
is exactly the set in the archive, in both directions. The MSVC `.lib` members carry their
full source paths (`obj/third_party/externals/<name>/...`), which is what makes the
derivation a measurement and not a guess; the Unix `.a` members carry bare gn target names,
so `gn_targets` below is the mapping back.
Deliberately absent, and verified absent in all six archives: FreeType, fontconfig, ICU and
HarfBuzz. The feature pin in the root `Cargo.toml` leaves `textlayout` off, so
`skia_use_icu` and `skia_use_harfbuzz` are both `false` and `embed-icudtl` is inert — the
prebuilt key `jpegd-jpege-pdf` has no icu component in it. FreeType and fontconfig appear on
Linux only as Skia's own ports (`typeface_freetype`, `fontmgr_fontconfig`) linking the
*system* libraries; their code is not in the archive and not in the release tarball.

prebuilt.license_file_sha256_comment: Over the file with CRLF normalised to LF: the Windows archives ship the same text with CRLF line endings.

skia.name: Skia
covers: Skia itself, and `modules/skcms`, whose `README.chromium` records `License: BSD` and whose sources defer to Skia's root LICENSE.

skia_own_gn_targets_comment: Every gn target in the six archives that is Skia's own code rather than something it
vendors. This list is what gives the four Unix legs the same strength the two Windows
legs get for free: an MSVC `.lib` member names its full source path, so a newly vendored
library announces itself as `third_party/externals/<something-new>`, but a Unix `.a`
member is a bare gn target name that says nothing about where it came from. Checking
every bare name against this list is what turns an unrecognised one into a failure
A Skia bump that adds a target will fail here. That is the intent: the failure is a
prompt to look at what moved and decide whether it is Skia's or somebody else's, which
is a judgment, not something a script can make. Note `wuffs`, `xml`, `jpeg_*` and
`png_*` — those are Skia's *codecs*, distinct from the `libwuffs`, `libexpat`,
`libjpeg*` and `libpng` targets that are the vendored libraries themselves.

bundled.name: Expat
bundled.why: `skia_use_expat` is unconditionally `true` in `skia-bindings`' gn args — Skia's XML parser, which the PDF backend's metadata path and `SkXmp` reach.

bundled.name: libjpeg-turbo
bundled.why: The `jpeg` feature in the root `Cargo.toml`'s Skia pin — `skia_use_libjpeg_turbo_decode` and `_encode`, the `jpegd-jpege` half of the prebuilt key.
bundled.obligation: The IJG License, clause (2): a distribution of executable code only must state in its accompanying documentation that "this software is based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group". THIRD-PARTY.md is that documentation and carries the sentence.

bundled.name: libpng
bundled.why: Not feature-gated: `skia_use_system_libpng` is false, so Skia's PNG codec — the one `render` writes frames with — links the vendored copy.

bundled.name: Wuffs
bundled.why: Skia's GIF decoder. Not feature-gated; present in all six archives.

bundled.name: zlib
bundled.revision_comment: Chromium's zlib fork, which is what Skia's DEPS pins; the SIMD targets below are that fork's additions.
bundled.why: PNG's deflate, and the PDF backend's stream compression. `skia_use_system_zlib` is false.

fonts_comment: Fonts the binary itself carries — not a project's, which belong to the project that vendors
them (ADR-0057), but Montagent's own. `ci/assert_third_party_attribution.py` checks each in
full: the file is present, its bytes hash to `sha256`, its notice is present, and `spdx` is
on ADR-0090's allowlist in both `about.toml` and `deny.toml`. `montagent-core`'s
`tests/chrome_face.rs` checks the same `sha256` against the bytes `include_bytes!` put in the
binary, so the attested file and the embedded one cannot be two different files.

fonts.name: JetBrains Mono NL Regular
fonts.why: The face Montagent draws its own chrome in — `frame`'s contact-sheet tile labels (#421, ADR-0098 §9) — embedded with `include_bytes!` so that neither the project's fonts nor the platform's decide how a label looks. It is never offered to a project's text.

system_libraries.name: FreeType
system_libraries.note: Dynamically linked from the system (`-lfreetype`). Skia's `typeface_freetype` port is in the archive; FreeType's own code is not, and no release tarball contains it.

system_libraries.name: fontconfig
system_libraries.note: Dynamically linked from the system (`-lfontconfig`), reached by Skia's `fontmgr_fontconfig` port. Montagent never asks it to resolve a family — `parley` is built without `fontique`'s `system` feature (see the root `Cargo.toml`) — but Skia's Linux link line requires the library present.

system_libraries.name: CoreText, CoreGraphics, CoreFoundation
system_libraries.note: Apple system frameworks, reached by Skia's `fontmgr_mac_ct` port.

system_libraries.name: GDI, DirectWrite, USP10
system_libraries.note: Windows system libraries, reached by Skia's `fontmgr_win` and `fontmgr_win_gdi` ports.
